raw_response:
I farm 6 mu, so I cannot spread money everywhere like a big grower. I will start from what has worked before and adjust a little, not make big changes. On my land, cabbage needs heavy base fertilizer and steady water, otherwise the head will not wrap tight. Chili and eggplant need feeding in stages, especially after fruit starts, because once they begin picking, they pull a lot from the soil. Kidney bean is lighter; if I push too much nitrogen, it will run vines and give me less pod, so I will keep nitrogen lower there. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage and not let the field go dry at key times. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get better stand and better marketable yield, especially for cabbage, chili, and eggplant. I will still keep kidney bean simpler and cheaper. For land arrangement, I will put 2 mu into spring cabbage, then after that I will follow that same 2 mu with summer chili. The other 4 mu I will split between eggplant and kidney bean so I have cash coming in at different times. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch yield drop, but I still have to watch the whole household budget, so I will not overdo the bean field.
